trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Spend a culinary afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine including pastéis de bacalhau, bifanas, ginjinha, and freshly made pastéis de nata from award-winning local chefs and vendors all under one roof.

experiences.name: Belém Historical Monuments & Custard Tart Tasting
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, exploring Portugal's Age of Discovery heritage. Conclude with a visit to the original Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, to taste the world-famous custard tarts fresh from the oven.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Metro (Linha Vermelha/Red Line) from Aeroporto station to central Lisbon for around €1.65 using a Viva Viagem card. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a gentle orientation walk through Baixa (Downtown Lisbon). Stroll along Rua Augusta, pass through the iconic Arco da Rua Augusta (exterior is free), and head down to Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River. Soak in the views of the river and the grand yellow square — completely free and a perfect first taste of Lisbon's history and grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic Alfama neighbourhood on foot. Wander the narrow cobblestone streets, admire the azulejo-tiled buildings, and climb up to the Miradouro das Portas do Sol for a stunning free sunset viewpoint over the rooftops and the Tagus River. Listen out for Fado music drifting from local tascas.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport or skip — you arrive at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget lunch near the airport or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) and a coffee at a local café in Baixa for around €3–5.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico or a similar local tasca in Alfama — try bacalhau à brás (salted cod) or caldo verde soup. Budget around €8–12 per person including a glass of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a rechargeable Viva Viagem card at the airport Metro station (€0.50 for the card). Load it with credit for all Metro, bus, and tram journeys throughout the trip. Keep your first evening light as travel fatigue may set in.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) — one of Lisbon's most iconic historical landmarks perched above the city. Entry is around €15 but offers sweeping panoramic views and centuries of Portuguese history from the Moorish period through the Age of Discovery. Arrive early (~9:30) to beat the crowds. Afterwards, explore the surrounding Mouraria neighbourhood, Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Alfama district for a deeper historical exploration. Visit the Lisbon Cathedral (Sé de Lisboa) — entry to the main nave is free. Walk through the Feira da Ladra flea market at Campo de Santa Clara (held Tuesdays and Saturdays — free to browse) to find vintage treasures and mingle with locals. Great for people-watching and local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Climb to Miradouro da Graça, one of the best and least touristy viewpoints in Lisbon, for golden hour views over the city. Then head back to Baixa or Bairro Alto for a relaxed evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local pastelaria (bakery) near the hotel for a galão (milky coffee) and a pastel de nata (custard tart) — budget around €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab a prato do dia (dish of the day) at a local restaurant in Mouraria — typically includes a main, bread, and a drink for €7–10.
meals.dinner: Explore Bairro Alto's budget-friendly eateries. Try A Tasca do Chico or similar — grilled sardines or pork with clams (carne de porco à alentejana) for €10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Alfama and the castle area involve steep, cobblestone streets. Saturday's Feira da Ladra is a highlight not to miss for local culture enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 15E or a bus out to the Belém district (about 6 km west of central Lisbon, reachable for ~€1.65 on the Viva Viagem card). Begin with the **Belém Historical Monuments & Custard Tart Tasting** experience — visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (€10 entry, one of Portugal's finest examples of Manueline architecture) and the iconic Tower of Belém (€6 entry) along the Tagus riverbank. Learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery and the voyages of Vasco da Gama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Belém. Visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) — the exterior and riverside promenade are free. Stop at the famous **Pastéis de Belém** bakery (the original since 1837) for the legendary custard tarts, dusted with cinnamon — just €1.30–1.50 each. Walk along the riverside gardens for free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and head to the Chiado neighbourhood. Browse the charming bookshops (including the historic Livraria Bertrand, the world's oldest operating bookshop — free to enter), and enjoy the lively Sunday evening atmosphere around Largo do Chiado.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hotel — coffee and toast with butter and jam (torrada) for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab a light lunch in Belém — prego no pão (steak sandwich) from a café near the monuments for €5–7, or picnic with local bread, cheese, and charcuterie from a nearby mini-market.
meals.dinner: Chiado area — try Zé da Mouraria or a similar tasca for traditional Portuguese food. Budget €10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is best explored on foot once you arrive. Sunday can be busy at the monuments — arrive at Jerónimos Monastery right when it opens at 10:00. The Pastéis de Belém queue moves fast despite appearances.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated museums, dedicated entirely to the Portuguese art of azulejo tile-making. Entry is €5 (reduced) and it's a must for history lovers. Located in a beautiful 16th-century convent in the Xabregas neighbourhood, easily reachable by bus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the **Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour** — spend a culinary afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré, sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine. Try petiscos (Portuguese tapas), fresh seafood, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and local cheeses from the market's many stalls. Budget around €15–20 for a satisfying self-guided tasting experience. Great for food lovers on a budget as you can mix and match small plates.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Cais do Sodré's vibrant Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho) — Lisbon's famous bar street — for an affordable drink. Try a Super Bock beer or a glass of vinho verde at one of the relaxed bars for €2–3. Enjoy the lively local nightlife atmosphere without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the hotel — coffee and a croissant or pastel de nata for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Light snack before or after the Tile Museum — a bifana or soup from a local café for €3–5.
meals.dinner: The Time Out Market afternoon covers most of your food intake — keep dinner light with a soup and bread at a neighbourhood tasca, or grab a francesinha (if you're adventurous — a hearty Portuguese sandwich) for €8–10.

day_by_day.notes: The Time Out Market is busiest at lunch and early evening — arriving around 14:00–15:00 on a Monday is ideal to avoid the biggest crowds. Keep your Viva Viagem card topped up for the bus to the Tile Museum.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa (€5.30 round trip, or free if you walk up to the top platform from the Carmo side) for panoramic rooftop views over Baixa and the Rossio. Then visit the hauntingly beautiful ruins of the Carmo Convent (Igreja do Carmo) — partially destroyed in the 1755 earthquake and left open to the sky as a monument to the disaster. Entry is €5 and it's one of Lisbon's most atmospheric historical sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon in the Príncipe Real neighbourhood — a charming, upscale-yet-relaxed area with a weekend market (Mercado de Príncipe Real on Saturdays, but the gardens are always open). Browse independent shops, admire grand 19th-century mansions, and visit the Jardim do Príncipe Real for a peaceful sit-down. Walk down to the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for one final sweeping view over Lisbon's rooftops — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Baixa-Chiado for a final farewell dinner in a traditional Portuguese restaurant. Celebrate the end of the trip with a full bacalhau dish or grilled fish, a carafe of house wine, and a dessert of arroz doce (sweet rice pudding) or a pastel de nata.

meals.breakfast: Final morning treat — sit down at a traditional café in Rossio square (Café Nicola or similar) for a galão and pastel de nata, soaking in the atmosphere. Budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pick up lunch at the Feira da Ladra market area (if Tuesday) or grab a prato do dia near Príncipe Real for €7–10.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell meal — a full sit-down dinner at a traditional tasca in Baixa or Chiado. Budget €15–20 per person including wine for a memorable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on May 20th or later, use this evening to pack and prepare. The Metro Red Line from Baixa-Chiado (change at São Sebastião) connects back to the airport. Allow 45–60 minutes travel time to the airport from central Lisbon. Keep your Viva Viagem card — it can be used for the airport journey.

trip_options.title: Classic Lisbon, Portugal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay, freshen up, and get oriented with a short stroll around the hotel neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Baixa-Chiado district on foot — a gentle, self-guided introduction to Lisbon. Ride the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic rooftop views over the city, then wander through Praça do Comércio along the Tagus riverfront to soak in the atmosphere without overloading on day one.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show: Join an early-evening guided walking tour through Alfama's narrow cobblestone streets, learning about the city's oldest neighborhood, Moorish heritage, and miradouros (viewpoints). End the night with an authentic Fado performance at a traditional casa de fado included in the tour.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastel de nata and galão (espresso with foamed milk) at a café near the airport or upon arrival in Baixa — try Café Nicola or a local pastelaria.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel after check-in — try A Cevicheria or a local tasca in Chiado for a €12–18 set lunch (menu do dia) with soup, main, and drink.
meals.dinner: Dinner is typically included or follows the Fado show experience in Alfama. If not, dine at Taberna da Rua das Flores — a beloved traditional Portuguese tavern with small plates around €15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the midday arrival. Pre-book the Alfama & Fado tour in advance as evening slots fill quickly, especially on weekends. Metro + bus are the most cost-effective transport options (€1.65/ride or a 24-hour Viva Viagem card for ~€6.45).

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Custard Tart Tasting: Take Tram 15E or a rideshare west to Belém. Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture celebrating Portugal's Age of Discovery. Explore the cloisters and the tomb of Vasco da Gama. Then walk to the iconic Tower of Belém on the Tagus riverfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém with the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) — climb to the top for sweeping river views. Stop at the nearby Museu de Arte, Arquitetura e Tecnologia (MAAT) for a quick modern contrast. End the afternoon with the essential custard tart tasting at Pastéis de Belém, the original home of the pastel de Belém since 1837.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the lively LX Factory, a repurposed industrial complex that hosts artisan shops, street art, and a vibrant Sunday market (open until ~20:00). Browse local crafts and enjoy the creative atmosphere before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local café — try a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) with coffee at a neighborhood pastelaria for under €5.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Belém at Vela Latina or Café In — traditional Portuguese dishes like bacalhau à brás (salt cod) or grilled sardines for €14–20. Alternatively, pick up snacks from the Pastéis de Belém bakery.
meals.dinner: Dinner at LX Factory's A Escola de Sabores or nearby O Mercado do Peixe — fresh seafood and Portuguese classics in a relaxed setting, budget €20–30 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is free on Sunday mornings until 14:00 — arrive early to beat the crowds. Belém is about 6 km from central Lisbon; Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira is the scenic and affordable option (~€3 with a Viva Viagem card).

day_by_day.morning: National Tile Museum & Azulejo Workshop: Head to the Museu Nacional do Azulejo, housed inside a stunning 16th-century convent in the Xabregas district. Spend the morning admiring Portugal's iconic blue-and-white tile tradition spanning five centuries, including a monumental 36-meter panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon. Participate in a hands-on azulejo painting workshop to create your own tile to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mouraria Neighborhood Food & History Walk: Join a small-group guided tour through Mouraria, Lisbon's historic Moorish quarter and the authentic birthplace of Fado. Discover hidden squares, centuries-old churches, street art, and the multicultural soul of the city while tasting local snacks and learning stories that don't appear in mainstream guidebooks.
day_by_day.evening: Spend a relaxed evening in the Intendente and Martim Moniz area — a revitalized multicultural neighborhood adjacent to Mouraria. Browse the Praça do Intendente, enjoy a drink at a terrace café, and take in the authentic local vibe away from tourist crowds.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel before heading out — try a café with ovos mexidos (scrambled eggs) and fresh orange juice for €6–8.
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included as tastings during the Mouraria Food & History Walk. If not, eat at Zé da Mouraria — a no-frills local restaurant beloved for its daily specials and affordable prices (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Chico in Mouraria or nearby Solar dos Presuntos in Avenida da Liberdade — both offer excellent traditional Portuguese cuisine with petiscos (tapas-style dishes) for €18–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tile Museum is closed on Mondays in some seasons — verify opening hours before visiting and consider booking the azulejo workshop at least 48 hours in advance as spots are limited. The Mouraria tour departs from Largo do Intendente — confirm exact meeting point when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) perched atop Lisbon's highest hill. Walk through the medieval ramparts, towers, and archaeological ruins with panoramic views over the city and the Tagus. Combine with a visit to the charming miradouro (viewpoint) of Portas do Sol and Santa Luzia nearby in Alfama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré for a culinary deep-dive into the best of Portuguese cuisine. Sample dishes from top chefs and producers — from seafood cataplana and bifanas to artisan cheeses and local wines. This is the perfect afternoon to graze and discover your favorite Portuguese flavors in one vibrant space.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Ribeira waterfront promenade from Cais do Sodré toward Santos. Stop for a sunset drink at a riverside bar or kiosk. Explore the Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho) for its lively nightlife atmosphere and colorful bar scene — perfect for a casual evening out.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at A Padaria Portuguesa — a beloved local bakery chain with fresh bread, pastries, and coffee for under €6.
meals.lunch: Lunch is the Time Out Market Food Tour itself — budget approximately €20–30 for a satisfying spread of tastings across multiple vendors including a glass of local wine or ginjinha.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Taberna Sal Grosso near Cais do Sodré or O Corvo wine bar in Intendente — natural wines and creative Portuguese petiscos for €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: São Jorge Castle tickets are approximately €15 for adults — book online to skip queues. The Time Out Market is free to enter; you pay per dish at each stall. Arrive at the market between 14:00–16:00 to avoid peak lunch crowds and get the best selection.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palácio Nacional de Sintra or the Convento dos Capuchos on a half-day trip to Sintra (30 minutes by train from Rossio Station, ~€2.35 each way). Sintra's fairy-tale palaces and lush forested hills make for a magical morning excursion. Alternatively, if staying in Lisbon, explore the elegant Avenida da Liberdade and visit the Museu Calouste Gulbenkian for world-class art in a beautiful garden setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lisbon and spend a leisurely afternoon in the Príncipe Real neighborhood — Lisbon's most elegant quarter. Browse the antique market at Praça das Flores (Saturdays) or the weekend organic market, explore independent boutiques, and visit the beautiful Jardim do Príncipe Real. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at local shops: azulejo tiles, local wine, tinned fish, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant to celebrate the trip. Splurge slightly within mid-range budget for the final night — enjoy a memorable meal showcasing the best of Portuguese cuisine before preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the Sintra train (departs Rossio ~09:00) — grab a croissant and espresso at a station café or hotel for €4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sintra at Tascas do Chico Elias — traditional Portuguese food near the palace for €12–18, or a picnic from a local bakery in the Sintra village square.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's Michelin-starred restaurant in Chiado, slightly above mid-range at €50–70 per person but worth it for the final night) or the more casual but excellent Taberna da Baixa for a traditional spread of bacalhau, grilled meats, and local wine at €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If visiting Sintra, purchase a combined palace ticket online in advance (€14–22 depending on sites) and go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. Trains run every 30–40 minutes from Rossio Station. Pack any fragile souvenirs like tiles carefully — dedicated souvenir shops near the Tile Museum offer professional wrapping. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening.

meals.lunch: Light lunch during the Mouraria food walk — sample authentic petiscos, local wines, and traditional street food curated by your guide.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Chico or Taberna da Rua das Flores — intimate, reservation-only Lisbon tabernas known for exceptional traditional Portuguese cooking, natural wines, and a deeply local atmosphere.

day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Sintra or return to Lisbon by mid-afternoon. If time allows, stop at the westernmost point of continental Europe, Cabo da Roca, for dramatic Atlantic Ocean cliffs and breathtaking scenery before heading back to Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lisbon's elegant Avenida da Liberdade — Lisbon's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard. Browse luxury flagship stores, then enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail at the sophisticated Bairro Alto Hotel bar before a special fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Lisbon City Stay — take time to enjoy a leisurely start before the Sintra excursion.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Incomum by Luis Santos in Sintra — a Michelin-recommended restaurant offering creative regional cuisine in a charming historic setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven Restaurant (1 Michelin star) — perched atop Parque Eduardo VII with sweeping panoramic views of Lisbon, offering refined contemporary cuisine and an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private driver and Sintra guide well in advance, especially for weekdays in May when crowds begin to build. Wear sturdy walking shoes for Sintra's hilly terrain. Pena Palace tickets should be pre-booked online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Lisbon — Revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore the elegant Príncipe Real district with its antique shops, art galleries, and the beautiful Jardim do Príncipe Real garden. Visit the Embaixada concept store (housed in a stunning Moorish Revival palace) for last-minute premium Portuguese gifts, artisan goods, and design pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Tagus River cruise — Embark on an exclusive private yacht or luxury boat tour along the Tagus River for a unique perspective of Lisbon's skyline, the 25 de Abril Bridge, and the Christ the King statue. Enjoy chilled Portuguese wine and local snacks on board as you glide past Belém's monuments from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Lisbon's most celebrated restaurants, savoring a final taste of Portugal's extraordinary culinary heritage before departure preparations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy the full spread, including seasonal fruits, local honey, artisan jams, and freshly baked pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solar dos Presuntos in Rossio — a Lisbon institution beloved for its exceptional cured meats, traditional bacalhau dishes, and warm, old-world hospitality.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Loco (1 Michelin star, Chef Alexandre Silva) — an avant-garde tasting menu experience celebrating the finest Portuguese ingredients in a bold, innovative style. An unforgettable final evening in Lisbon.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is in the evening. Confirm private transfer to the airport in advance. The Tagus River cruise should be booked ahead — private charters offer the most flexible and luxurious experience. Consider purchasing a bottle of premium Vintage Port or Ginjinha as a parting gift from Portugal.
